brief: GS TMT Specialist Sales morning note covering earnings previews, M&A and flow commentary across TMT. GIR raises TSMC's 2027E/2028E capex forecasts to $85bn/$98bn from $78bn/$82bn on equipment inflation and Texas expansion, while holding 2026E capex at $64bn. N2 ramp dilutes 3Q/4Q26 gross margin to 67.5%/67.3%, but full-year GM still holds near 67%, supporting raised EPS forecasts of 110/150/195 for 2026-28. Desk feedback frames TSMC's 17-18x FY27 valuation as cheap against other AI names trading above 20x. SAP's organic cloud backlog guidance (c.23% CCB growth, 22% 4Q exit rate, c.24% FY26 cloud growth) is unchanged. Informa is buying faster-growing Clarion from Blackstone for £2.24bn, funded by financing, a £940m equity raise and a paused buyback, while separating slower-growing Taylor & Francis, so the desk reads this as buying growth and funding it by shedding the slow asset. Deutsche Telekom frames AI as a cost opportunity, targeting €1.1bn savings by 2027 and €2.5bn by 2030, but analysts stayed skeptical it reaches earnings because guidance was not raised. Brazil's election outcome beat market fears, squeezing EWZ shorts (+13%), while US long/short net leverage sits near five-year lows despite indices near highs, meaning further upside would force buying.
